figure: FIGURE 7.6 — 'Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning (canonical 70B, FP16 unless noted)'
issue: The five-line note block below the chart and the red annotation 'full fine-tune exceeds an 8xH100 box: needs multi-node or offload' are set in small type, below the caption's size, and the note block carries the figure's most important scoping statements (what is and is not included). At print size these are the hardest text on the page to read.
evidence: The note block ('Each bar is a conditional floor ... Activation, microbatch/sequence, and offload/checkpointing are NOT included (Table 7-2) ...') is visibly smaller than the caption below it; the red annotation above the full-fine-tune bar is likewise small.
acceptance_test: Confirm the note block and the red annotation are >= 8 pt at print size; if not, enlarge them or move the scoping statements into the caption, where they are already partly restated.

issue: The caption states the per-request KV price is "24.9 GB/request max-fp16 KV (0.5K max context, per Fig 7.6)". 0.5K = 500 tokens; at the book's canonical 2.62 MB/token FP16 KV that is 1.31 GB/request, not 24.9 GB. The figure's own arithmetic (436 / 24.9 = 17.5) and FIG 7.8 on the facing page (the identical 24.9 GB block labelled "9.5K context") both require 9.5K tokens: 24.9 GB / 2.62 MB per token = 9,504 tokens. As printed, the caption's stated context length is wrong by a factor of 19 and a reader who recomputes from it gets C ~ 333 instead of 17.
evidence: Caption on PDF p.154 / printed p.134. FIG 7.8 on PDF p.155 / printed p.135 labels the same 24.9 GB KV block "9.5K context" and derives 32K -> 84 GB and 128K -> 335 GB from the same 2.62 MB/token, which is mutually consistent only at 9.5K. 24.9 GB / 2.62 MB = 9,504 tokens.
acceptance_test: Caption reads "9.5K max context" (or "9,504 tokens"); a reader recomputing 9.5K x 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB reproduces the figure's 17.5 -> 17 exactly; the string "0.5K" no longer appears anywhere in the Ch 7 KV-price derivation.

issue: In the figure's arithmetic line the operator between "436 GB" and "24.9 GB" is not legible as division at the supplied render size; it reads as "+". If it is "+", the figure asserts 436 + 24.9 = 17.5, which is false. The line immediately above reads "in-flight = KV budget / KV per request" and the caption says "KV budget / the per-request KV price sets concurrency", so the intent is division; the glyph simply must not be confusable with a plus at print size.
evidence: Rendered PDF p.154 / printed p.134, line "~ 436 GB [op] 24.9 GB = 17.5 -> ~17 requests"; the line above reads "in-flight = KV budget / KV per request"; caption reads "KV budget / the per-request KV price sets concurrency".
acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the operator is unambiguously a division sign (or the line is rewritten "17.5 = 436 GB / 24.9 GB"); no reader at print size can read it as "+".

issue: The figure title says "640 GB pool" and draws one contiguous bar, which invites the reading that 640 GB is a single freely-allocatable pool. The caption's own aggregate-feasibility caveat says the opposite: 640 GB is an aggregate across eight 80 GB H100s and per-rank fit must be validated separately. The figure carries no rank structure, so the caveat exists only in prose and the figure actively contradicts it.
evidence: PDF p.154 / printed p.134: title "Concurrency budget - one 8xH100 host" with "640 GB pool"; caption "640 GB is an aggregate across eight 80 GB H100s, not a freely-allocatable heap - per-rank fit must be validated separately". Contrast FIG 7.8 (PDF p.155), which does draw the 8 x 80 GB rank structure.
acceptance_test: FIG 7.7 either draws the eight 80 GB rank boundaries (as FIG 7.8 does) or its title/annotation states "aggregate across 8 ranks - not one allocatable pool"; the caption caveat is then visible in the figure, not only in prose.

issue: The caption's central teaching point - "floor 17, not 18" - is asserted rather than shown. The caption says "the faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots", but at print size those rules are not resolvable, and the band does not show the ~12.7 GB that remains after 17 slots (17 x 24.9 = 423.3 GB of the 436 GB band), which is precisely why the 18th slot does not fit (18 x 24.9 = 448.2 GB > 436 GB).
evidence: PDF p.154 / printed p.134: caption "C = 17 concurrent (floor 17, not 18: the faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots)"; the orange KV band shows only a dot texture at print size.
acceptance_test: The KV band shows 17 countable slot divisions plus a visibly distinct leftover segment (~12.7 GB) labelled as such, and the slot rules are legible at 8 pt print size; a reader can see why 18 does not fit without doing arithmetic.

issue: Caption: "FP8 (~12.45 GB/request) roughly raises it to ~35.5". 436 / 12.45 = 35.0, so the stated value is off by ~0.5, and the double hedge ("roughly" plus "~") is redundant.
evidence: PDF p.154 / printed p.134 caption; 436 / 12.45 = 35.02.
acceptance_test: Caption reads "~35" (or "35.0"), consistent with the floor rule applied to the FP16 case.

issue: The bar has no scale endpoints: nothing marks 0 or 640 GB at its ends, so the reader cannot read the bar quantitatively without trusting the title. The segment widths are in fact accurate (140/64/436 of 640), which is wasted information.
evidence: PDF p.154 / printed p.134: bar spans "140 GB weights | ~64 GB | ~436 GB KV budget" with no axis or endpoint ticks; measured segment proportions match 140/640, 64/640, 436/640.
acceptance_test: The bar carries "0" and "640 GB" endpoint labels (or a one-line scale note), so segment widths are readable as GB.

issue: The figure's own note says "Bar heights are not to scale (GB)", but the drawn bars are proportional to the stated GB values. Measured from the rendered page: the 9.5K bar is ~75 px tall for 229 GB, the 32K bar ~95 px for 288 GB, the 128K bar ~165 px for 539 GB, i.e. 0.327 / 0.330 / 0.306 px per GB - consistent within ~7%. The note therefore tells the reader not to read the figure quantitatively when the quantitative reading is the entire point of the "Memory Tetris" comparison (and the light 80 GB rules are in fact a working scale).
evidence: PDF p.155 / printed p.135: note under the bars "The baseline (weights + runtime) is fixed; only the KV cache grows with context. Bar heights are not to scale (GB)."; bar labels "~ 229 GB used", "~ 288 GB used", "~ 539 GB used"; the 80 GB rules and the 640 GB dashed ceiling are drawn to the same scale.
acceptance_test: Either the note is removed (the drawing is already to scale) or the bars are redrawn to a stated non-linear scale with the note explaining why; the reader is never told the figure is non-quantitative while it is quantitative.

issue: The caption refers to "the P1xP xKV block", a symbol defined nowhere in the figure, the caption, or the visible chapter text; it reads as a mangling of "the KV block".
evidence: PDF p.155 / printed p.135 caption: "the P1xP xKV block is the only block that grows".
acceptance_test: The caption names the block using a term defined in the figure (e.g. "the KV cache block"); "P1xP xKV" does not appear anywhere in the book.

issue: The subtitle "(light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)" describes horizontal rules as rank boundaries. The rules are a capacity scale (80 GB steps); a rank boundary in a stacked bar would be a vertical division into eight 80 GB segments. As written, the reader is told horizontal rules mark ranks.
evidence: PDF p.155 / printed p.135: subtitle "(light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)" above a plot whose only rules are horizontal.
acceptance_test: Subtitle reads e.g. "light rules = 80 GB steps (one H100 rank's capacity)", or the figure adds vertical rank divisions; the phrase "rank boundaries" is used only for an actual rank division.

issue: Red is used for two different semantic roles in the same figure: the 640 GB capacity ceiling (red dashed rule) and the KV quantity labels ("KV 24.9 GB", "KV 84 GB", "KV 335 GB"). The reader cannot tell whether a red element is a limit or a quantity.
evidence: PDF p.155 / printed p.135: red dashed rule "640 GB = 8x 80 GB ranks" and red bold KV labels above each bar.
acceptance_test: One colour per semantic role in the figure (e.g. ceiling in red, KV labels in the KV swatch colour), or the KV labels are moved inside the KV blocks.

issue: The takeaway sentence conflates two different claims: "the P1xP xKV block is the only block that grows, consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget at 17.5 -> 17 concurrent". At 128K the KV block is 335 GB, i.e. it does not consume the 436 GB budget, and the 17-concurrent figure belongs to the 9.5K case only. As written the takeaway reads as if all three bars consume the full KV budget at 17 concurrent.
evidence: PDF p.155 / printed p.135 caption vs. the figure's own bars: 9.5K -> KV 24.9 GB, 32K -> KV 84 GB, 128K -> KV 335 GB, against a ~436 GB KV budget.
acceptance_test: The takeaway names which bar the 17-concurrent figure belongs to and states that at 128K the KV block is 335 GB of the 436 GB budget (one 128K request fits, not 17).

figure: FIGURE 8.1 (Where inference computation and data movement actually live)
issue: The "L2 cache" box's sub-label renders as the single word "byte". That is not a meaningful descriptor and breaks the parallel structure of the other sub-labels ("fastest - smallest", "arithmetic", "on-chip - close", "large - slower"); it reads as a truncated or placeholder string. Related: "shared mem (SRAM)" is labelled "on-chip - close", but registers are also on-chip, so the label does not distinguish the two tiers.
evidence: PDF p.161 / printed p.141, left column, fourth box: "L2 cache" with sub-label "byte".
acceptance_test: The L2 sub-label is a meaningful qualifier consistent with the other tiers (e.g. "on-chip - larger" or "MB-scale"), and the SRAM sub-label distinguishes SRAM from registers.

issue: The red annotation block ("capacity grows / speed drops / distance grows") occupies the same horizontal band as the vertical ladder arrow, and its third line appears to touch or cross the arrow shaft - the arrow being the figure's only visual anchor for the speed/capacity gradient.
evidence: PDF p.161 / printed p.141, right column: the three-line red annotation sits immediately left of the vertical double-headed arrow whose top and bottom labels ("small - fast - close", "large - slow") are centred on the same shaft.
acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the red annotation and the arrow shaft do not overlap; the annotation is moved clear of the shaft (or the shaft moved) with at least 4 pt of white space.

issue: Compute (blue, solid) and interconnect (green, solid) are distinguished by colour alone; memory is additionally distinguished by a dotted texture. In grayscale the blue tensor-core box and the green interconnect boxes are close in value, so the three-way grouping degrades to two.
evidence: PDF p.161 / printed p.141: legend "compute" (solid blue), "memory" (solid orange swatch), "interconnect" (solid green); the tensor-core box and both interconnect-tier boxes are solid fills.
acceptance_test: A grayscale proof of the page still lets a reader assign every box to compute / memory / interconnect without relying on hue (e.g. a distinct texture or border for one of the two solid-fill groups).

issue: The mapping from the left-hand resource stack to the middle "what runs here ->" column is purely positional - there are no leader lines or shared row rules - so the reader must scan horizontally to pair "registers" with "tile values in flight", "HBM (GPU memory)" with "model weights + KV cache", and so on. That pairing is the figure's content.
evidence: PDF p.161 / printed p.141: left column of seven coloured boxes, middle column of seven text labels, no connectors between them.
acceptance_test: Each middle label is unambiguously tied to its left-hand box (leader lines or a shared row rule), and the pairing can be read without horizontal scanning.

issue: The legend swatch for "memory" is solid orange, but every memory box in the stack is drawn with a dotted texture; the legend therefore does not show the encoding the reader must actually use to identify memory.
evidence: PDF p.161 / printed p.141: legend row "memory" with a solid orange swatch; the registers / shared mem / L2 / HBM boxes are orange with a white dot pattern.
acceptance_test: The legend swatch reproduces the texture used in the figure, or the figure's memory boxes are solid-filled to match the legend.

figure: FIGURE 8.2 (Per-GPU roofline: dense FP16, one H100 vs one H200)
issue: The two ridge labels appear transposed. As rendered, the blue (H100) curve carries the label "H200 ridge = 295" and the red (H200) curve carries "H100 ridge = 206". The book's own arithmetic gives the opposite: H100 ridge = 989 TFLOPS / 3.35 TB/s = 295 FLOP/byte; H200 ridge = 989 TFLOPS / 4.8 TB/s = 206 FLOP/byte. The body text on the facing page states this explicitly, so a reader who trusts the figure learns the wrong ridge geometry for both GPUs and sees the figure contradict the prose one page earlier.
evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: annotations "H200 ridge = 295" (blue) and "H100 ridge = 206" (red); legend "H100 FP16 (3.35 TB/s)" / "H200 FP16 (4.8 TB/s)"; PDF p.168 / printed p.148 prose: "the ridge point for dense FP16 on H100 is ~295 FLOP/byte (989 / 3.35) and ~206 on H200 (989 / 4.8)". The drawn knees are correct (blue knee right of red knee), so the error is in the labels.
acceptance_test: Rendered figure shows "H100 ridge = 295" in the H100 (blue) colour adjacent to the blue curve's knee and "H200 ridge = 206" in the H200 (red) colour adjacent to the red curve's knee; figure and printed p.148 agree; each label sits within one label-height of its own curve.

issue: The prefill marker does not appear to sit at the arithmetic intensity its own label states. The label reads "prefill 9.2K (intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte)", but on the log x-axis (10^-1 ... 10^4) the vertical dashed prefill line appears to fall between 10^2 and 10^3 (roughly 5 x 10^2 FLOP/byte), not at 9.2 x 10^3, which would place it immediately left of the 10^4 tick. Either the marker or the label is wrong. The qualitative claim (prefill right of the ridge, on the compute-bound plateau) survives either placement, so this is a quantitative error, not a conclusion error.
evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: x-axis ticks 10^-1, 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, 10^4; the red dashed vertical line is drawn well left of the 10^4 tick while its annotation states "intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte"; the caption separately says "the plotted prefill (9.2K input) ... points are illustrative operating points".
acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the vertical dashed prefill line is at log10 = 3.96 (9.2 x 10^3 FLOP/byte), immediately left of the 10^4 tick and clear of the "compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS" annotation; if the plotted intensity is not 9.2K, the label is corrected to the plotted value and the caption's "prefill (9.2K input)" wording is reconciled.

issue: The prefill point's arithmetic intensity is quoted without its denominator. 9.2K FLOP/byte is obtained by dividing prefill FLOPs (1,288 TFLOP) by weight bytes only (140 GB); including the KV write traffic for 9.2K tokens (~24.1 GB) gives ~7.9K FLOP/byte, and including activation traffic lowers it further. The figure's caption insists on separating "a theoretical bound ... from a measured latency", so the denominator belongs in the annotation.
evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: annotation "prefill 9.2K (intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte)"; 1,288 TFLOP / 140 GB = 9,200 FLOP/byte; 1,288 TFLOP / (140 + 24.1) GB ~ 7,850 FLOP/byte.
acceptance_test: The annotation or caption states the denominator ("weights only"), and if the KV-write-inclusive value is used the plotted x-position is updated to match; the reader can reproduce the plotted intensity from the stated inputs.
